topics.name: MKUltra
topics.description: CIA program of covert human experimentation (1953–c. 1973). Chosen as the seed topic because it has a rock-solid documented core and a real fringe of overreach — the full range of evidence tiers gets exercised.

topics.name: COINTELPRO
topics.description: FBI program (1956–1971) of covert surveillance, infiltration, and disruption of domestic political organizations. Companion topic to MKUltra: same declassification era, exposed by the 1971 Media, PA burglary and documented by the Church Committee.

topics.name: The Replication Crisis
topics.description: Whether published psychology findings survive independent replication (2011–present). Chosen by the builder as a topic personally cared about: it is this tool's own subject — what survives scrutiny — applied to a scientific literature.

claims.text: Project MKUltra existed: a CIA program of covert experimentation on human subjects, run from 1953 into the early 1970s, approved under DCI Allen Dulles, directed by Sidney Gottlieb, with Richard Helms as its key internal sponsor.
claims.placement_reason: Established by primary government documents and sworn testimony (Church Committee, 1977 Senate hearings, surviving CIA financial records). Has survived public challenge continuously since 1975.

claims.text: The Church Committee (1975–76) and the August 1977 Senate hearings publicly exposed MKUltra, after ~20,000 pages of misfiled financial records were located in 1977.
claims.placement_reason: The exposure is itself the primary record: committee reports and the published hearing transcript.

claims.text: In January 1973, on the order of CIA Director Richard Helms, most MKUltra records were destroyed by the CIA.
claims.placement_reason: Acknowledged under oath by CIA leadership in the 1977 hearings and documented by the Church Committee.

claims.text: Frank Olson, a U.S. Army scientist, was covertly dosed with LSD by CIA personnel in November 1953 and died nine days later in a fall from the Statler Hotel in New York. The government acknowledged the dosing; Congress compensated his family by private law in 1976.
claims.placement_reason: Documented by the Rockefeller Commission and settled by act of Congress — primary and legal records, not reporting.

claims.text: Because of the 1973 destruction, the surviving financial records give an incomplete picture: the full scope and content of MKUltra's ~150 subprojects cannot be fully reconstructed.
claims.placement_reason: The incompleteness is documented in the 1977 hearings; how much is missing, and what it contained, remains credibly disputed — well-supported, but not Core.

claims.text: Ewen Cameron's "psychic driving" and de-patterning experiments at Montreal's Allan Memorial Institute received MKUltra funding (Subproject 68) and left patients with lasting harm.
claims.placement_reason: CIA funding and patient harm are documented (Orlikow settlement, surviving subproject records); the precise share of CIA versus Canadian government responsibility remains credibly disputed.

claims.text: Ted Kaczynski's participation in Henry Murray's abusive psychological study at Harvard (1959–62) connects him to MKUltra.
claims.placement_reason: The Murray study and Kaczynski's participation are documented; the study's tie to MKUltra funding is circumstantial and has never been shown in primary records. Path inward: a surviving subproject financial record naming the Murray study.

claims.text: Experimenting on unwitting human subjects, as MKUltra did, was a profound moral wrong.
claims.placement_reason: A value judgment resting on a documented factual record. Barred from Core by rule — moral claims never sit in the factual core — but the facts beneath it are Core-grade.

claims.text: MKUltra never really ended — it continues today under other names.
claims.placement_reason: Stated faithfully. No primary documentation of continuation after the program's termination in the early 1970s; the only offered source is anonymous, which carries zero weight. The 1973 record destruction explains missing history — it is not evidence of a present-day program. Path inward: verifiable post-1973 documents showing continuation.

claims.text: MKUltra proves the government still treats citizens as expendable test subjects.
claims.placement_reason: Framing claim: it converts a documented historical program into a present-tense characterization of intent. The historical facts are established; the present-tense "still treats" carries no evidence of its own.

claims.text: MKUltra evolved into a fully operational present-day system of total mind control over the population, via implants and electromagnetic weapons.
claims.placement_reason: Established: MKUltra existed (1953–early 1970s), experimented on unwitting subjects, was exposed by the Church Committee and 1977 hearings, and most of its records were destroyed in 1973. — The present-day total-mind-control remainder is checked and failed: its only supporting source is the claimant's own publication (zero weight by rule), and the primary record documents a program that could not achieve reliable behavioral control. Debunked — kept visible, not fleshed out.

claims.text: MKUltra was one battle in a spiritual war over humanity's souls.
claims.placement_reason: Not resolvable by documents, observation, or data in either direction. Routed off the radial axis by rule — ranking it "weak" would secretly assert its negation as "strong".

claims.text: COINTELPRO existed: an FBI counterintelligence program (1956–1971) that covertly surveilled, infiltrated, and worked to disrupt and discredit domestic political organizations, from the Communist Party USA to civil-rights, Black-liberation, and New Left groups.
claims.placement_reason: Established by the FBI's own released files and the Church Committee's investigation — primary government documents, publicly challenged and standing since 1971.

claims.text: The March 1971 burglary of the FBI's Media, Pennsylvania office by the Citizens' Commission to Investigate the FBI took internal files that, once passed to the press, first exposed COINTELPRO to the public.
claims.placement_reason: The stolen files are themselves the primary record; their authenticity was confirmed by the FBI and the subsequent investigations.

claims.text: The FBI targeted Martin Luther King Jr. with extensive surveillance and, in 1964, sent him an anonymous letter and tape urging him toward suicide.
claims.placement_reason: Documented by the Church Committee from FBI files; the anonymous letter itself is in the released record.

claims.text: J. Edgar Hoover formally terminated COINTELPRO in April 1971, weeks after the Media burglary put the program at risk of exposure.
claims.placement_reason: Hoover's termination directive survives in the released files and is documented by the Church Committee.

claims.text: The FBI's COINTELPRO campaign against the Black Panther Party contributed to the December 1969 police raid in which Chicago police killed Fred Hampton.
claims.placement_reason: An FBI informant's floor plan and the Bureau's Panther operations are documented, and the families' civil suit ended in a substantial settlement; the precise degree of FBI direction of the raid itself remains credibly disputed — well-supported, not Core.

claims.text: COINTELPRO-style FBI disruption was a decisive cause of the American Indian Movement's internal collapse in the mid-1970s.
claims.placement_reason: FBI activity around AIM and Pine Ridge is documented, but COINTELPRO formally ended in 1971 and the causal claim about AIM's collapse rests on inference from partial records. Path inward: released FBI files showing a directed disruption program against AIM comparable to the documented COINTELPRO operations.

claims.text: COINTELPRO never ended — domestic political policing continues today as the same program under new names.
claims.placement_reason: Stated faithfully. The program's 1971 termination is documented; later documented abuses (which are real) are not evidence that the same program continued. The only offered source is anonymous — zero weight. Path inward: verifiable post-1971 documents showing a successor program with the same charter and chain of command.

claims.text: Every prominent activist death since 1968 was an FBI assassination carried out under COINTELPRO.
claims.placement_reason: Established: COINTELPRO existed (1956–1971), targeted lawful domestic groups, and in documented cases contributed to deaths (e.g., Fred Hampton). — The universal version is checked and failed: its only support is the claimants' own publications (zero weight), and the investigated record — which documents real abuses in detail — contradicts a program of universal assassination. Debunked; kept visible, not fleshed out.

claims.text: COINTELPRO was the state's war on the nation's soul.
claims.placement_reason: Not resolvable by documents or observation in either direction. Off the radial axis by rule.

claims.text: Large-scale preregistered replication projects (2011–2018) found that a substantial fraction of published psychology findings — roughly 40–60% depending on the sample — do not replicate when rerun by independent labs.
claims.placement_reason: Three independent, preregistered, multi-lab projects published their own primary records and converge; the figure is stated as a range because the samples differ. Publicly challenged since 2015 and standing.

claims.text: The ego-depletion effect — willpower as a depletable resource that later tasks exhaust — failed to replicate in two large preregistered multi-lab projects, with pooled effects near zero.
claims.placement_reason: Two independent multi-lab primary records converge on a near-zero effect. The original authors’ published methodological objection is attached as contradicting evidence, honestly — and while that credible dispute stands, this stays out of Core. Inner is what it earns.

claims.text: Undisclosed analytic flexibility ("researcher degrees of freedom") can manufacture statistically significant evidence for a false conclusion — demonstrated in 2011 by "showing", with conventional methods, that listening to a song changed subjects' ages.
claims.placement_reason: The demonstration is its own primary record and has been reproduced conceptually many times, but one primary document is what exists — Inner is what one primary document earns under this tool's bar, and Core's two-independent-records requirement is the right kind of strict.

claims.text: The hormonal and risk-taking effects of "power posing" failed to replicate in a five-times-larger study, and the original paper's first author publicly disavowed the effect in 2016; only the self-reported feeling of power holds up.
claims.placement_reason: A higher-powered replication and the first author's own against-interest disavowal support the failure; the senior author's published p-curve defense is attached as contradicting evidence and keeps this at Inner while the dispute stands.

claims.text: Questionable research practices — p-hacking, selective reporting, optional stopping — are the primary cause of the replication failures.
claims.placement_reason: The prevalence of the practices is documented (survey with truth-telling incentives), and the mechanism is proven possible (the false-positive demonstration) — but "primary cause" is a causal attribution none of the attached sources measures. Deliberately placed at Middle although the evidence count would pass Inner: the sources establish plausibility, not the causal share. Path inward: studies that trace failed replications to specific documented practices in the original papers.

claims.text: "Most published research findings are false" — in most scientific fields, the majority of published claims are false.
claims.placement_reason: Stated faithfully. The 2005 origin paper is a theoretical model of publication incentives, not an empirical audit — it argues the claim rather than measures it, so citing it is close to restating the claim. The replication projects sample specific psychology literatures and are consistent with high false rates there, but do not establish "most, in most fields". Path inward: preregistered field-wide audits across disciplines.

claims.text: The replication crisis proves psychology is empty — nothing the field has ever produced can be trusted.
claims.placement_reason: Established: Large preregistered multi-lab projects (2011–2018) found replication rates of roughly 36–62% in the sampled literatures; undisclosed analytic flexibility demonstrably manufactures false positives; several famous effects failed high-powered replication. — The nihilist remainder is checked and failed: the same audits that document the failures document the substantial fraction that replicated — large effects most reliably — and the only support offered for "nothing can be trusted" is the claimants' own posts (zero weight). Debunked; kept visible, not fleshed out.

claims.text: The replication crisis shows psychology was never a real science.
claims.placement_reason: Framing claim: it converts a documented measurement problem into a verdict on the field's nature. The documented record (large-scale self-audit and reform) is, if anything, science behaving as science. No sources offered.

claims.text: Knowingly presenting p-hacked analyses as confirmatory findings is scientific misconduct — morally closer to fabrication than to error.
claims.placement_reason: A value judgment, barred from Core by rule regardless of sourcing. It rests on the documented fact that undisclosed flexibility manufactures false positives — the factual base is attached; the moral weight is the claim's own.

claims.text: What the replication failures ultimately reveal is that the mind is not the kind of thing empirical method can capture.
claims.placement_reason: Not resolvable by replication data in either direction — any replication rate is compatible with it. Off the radial axis by rule.

kernels.gap_establishes: The program was exposed and publicly documented: the Church Committee (1975–76) and the August 1977 Senate hearings.
kernels.gap_asserts_beyond: That what was exposed continued and matured into total mind control — the exposure record documents a terminated program and ends in 1977.

kernels.gap_asserts_beyond: Universal authorship of deaths — that every prominent activist death since 1968 was an FBI assassination, far past documented disruption.

kernels.gap_establishes: The FBI's COINTELPRO campaign against the Black Panther Party contributed to the December 1969 death of Fred Hampton — one documented case.
kernels.gap_asserts_beyond: Generalizing one documented contribution into FBI assassination of every prominent activist death since 1968.
kernels.gap_path_inward: the standard of evidence that documented the Hampton case, met separately for each further claimed death
